summary: A one-paragraph announcement that the time limit for anonymous sampling use of the Multics system over the ARPANET was raised from one CPU minute to five, so that a real experiment could fit in one session. It is a service notice, not a protocol.

eli5.summary: A school computer that lets visitors try it out said visitors could now use it for five minutes instead of one.

subtitle: Increasing the time limit for trial use of a remote computer system.

tldr.problem: Researchers trying out MIT's Multics system over the network had only one CPU minute for a trial session, which was too short for meaningful experiments.
tldr.mechanism: MIT increased the trial usage limit from one CPU minute to five, and added internal speedups to make experiments feasible within a session.
tldr.outcome: The extended time allowed users to run substantive experiments without needing to reconnect, improving the trial experience.

today: RFC 450 documents a service adjustment for an early timesharing system. Multics is no longer in operation, and remote trial access practices have evolved significantly.

sections.title: The Sampling Timeout Change
sections.content: RFC 450 announces a change to the MIT Multics system's remote access policy. Multics allowed anonymous sampling (trial) use over the ARPANET network, but the timeout on these sessions was only one CPU minute. This time limit was too brief for users to run real experiments or evaluate the system properly.
sections.eli5: MIT's remote computer system let anyone try it over the network, but only for one minute.

sections.title: The Improvement
sections.content: In response to user demand and thanks to a budget adjustment, MIT raised the sampling timeout to five CPU minutes. Additionally, internal performance improvements made the system faster, allowing users to accomplish more within a single session. The combined effect was that visitors could now conduct meaningful experiments and evaluations during their trial period.
sections.eli5: MIT gave users five minutes instead of one, and made the system run faster, so users could actually try real work.

sections.title: Supporting Remote Access
sections.content: This change reflects the growing importance of remote access to computing resources over the ARPANET. Providing adequate trial periods encouraged sites to use network-accessible systems and helped build a culture of resource sharing among research institutions. The timeout increase demonstrates how operational adjustments to remote services could improve their utility and adoption.
sections.eli5: Letting people try the computer for longer made more researchers want to use it over the network.
